title: Two first knots under one count and under the fewest counts
claim: S1: a start of knots with no common neighbour grows as independent pieces, one per start knot, each a single seed on its open distinctions. Theorem 2: under one count c >= 2 the growth runs exactly when every start knot has 0, 1 or c open distinctions, else stalls at the earliest r(l, c); so a three-place and a four-place first knot apart or sharing one distinction cannot grow under any count; Corollary 2.1: the same relation grows at c = 4 or 2 by presentation. S3: under the fewest counts, separate knots close; two knots sharing one distinction grow two copies of N^2 forever for every pair of sizes. S4: cheapness prefers the least admissible count. Proposition 4 (added after the census): m >= 3 mutually touching knots of m + 1 places grow m-dimensionally under the fewest counts.
